titleEn: The Glory of Kings — Mary, Daughter of David (ch. 71)
source: Carl Bezold, Kebra Nagast: Die Herrlichkeit der Könige (Munich, 1905), ch. 71 — public domain. Geʿez text as in Ran HaCohen's Unicode edition of Bezold (tau.ac.il/~hacohen/KN, from Michal Jerabek's 1995 digitization), archived and checked against Bezold's printed page. Per-sign transliteration derived mechanically from Unicode; word-level romanization auto-generated (schwa-reduced) and approximate. Transliteration convention: ś = ሠ-series, ʿ = ዐ-series, ə = 6th order, 1st order ä, 4th order a. Translations made fresh from the Geʿez; Dillmann's Lexicon (1865) the lexical aid.
about: The text draws the conclusion of the genealogy: Mary, like Joseph, is of David’s house, and Joseph was betrothed to her as a kinsman. It gives words from the Gospel addressed to Joseph (compare Matthew 1:20) and passes into a creed-like praise of the Word born of her, who saved his creation and made the faithful his heirs in heaven.

sentences.i: Chapter 71: Concerning Mary, Daughter of David
sentences.n: Chapter heading. በእንተ ‘concerning’ + ማርያም ‘Mary’ + ወለተ, the construct of ወለት ‘daughter’, + ዳዊት ‘David’: ‘daughter-of David’. The number ፸፩ is 71, spoken ሰብዓ ወአሐዱ (säbʿa wä-ʾäḥadu). The previous part ended by tracing Joseph’s descent and the rule of marrying among one’s kin; this chapter turns to Mary.

sentences.l: And-on-account-of-this (it) was-known that Mary daughter-of David she (is), and-Joseph-too son-of David he (is);
sentences.i: And so it is known that Mary is a daughter of David, and that Joseph too is a son of David;
sentences.n: ወበእንተዝኬ is ወ- ‘and’ + በእንተ ‘on account of’ + ዝ ‘this’ + the enclitic -ኬ (emphatic (?)), ‘and for this reason’. ተዐውቀ is the tä-stem (passive) perfect 3ms of ዐወቀ ‘know’ (?), ‘it was/has become known’; I render it ‘it is known’, as the house rendering of ተብህለ has it; the ከመ-clause is its content. ይእቲ ‘she (is)’ and ውእቱ ‘he (is)’ are pronouns serving as the copula, as the glossary has it. -ኒ in ወዮሴፍኒ is the enclitic ‘too, also’. Joseph’s Davidic descent was set out at the end of ch. 70; here the text asserts the same of Mary, and the next unit draws the consequence for the betrothal.

sentences.l: and-on-account-of-this was-betrothed Mary to-Joseph, her-kinsman, as it-was-said in-the-Gospel: O Joseph son-of David, do-not-fear taking-her to-Mary your-betrothed, for what is-born from-her from-spirit holy word-of God he (is);
sentences.i: And for this reason Mary was betrothed to Joseph, her kinsman, as it is said in the Gospel: “O Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take her, Mary, your betrothed, for that which is born of her, of the Holy Spirit, is the Word of God.”
sentences.n: ተፍኅረት I read as the tä-stem (passive) perfect 3fs of ፈኀረ ‘betroth’ (?), ‘she was betrothed’; the verb is not confirmed (ch. 70 has ዘፈኀራ, active), and the spelling with 6th-order ፍ is not the regular passive ተፈኀረት, so the parse is from the context (?). ፍኅርትከ ‘your betrothed’ is probably the related noun ፍኅርት (?) + -ከ ‘your (ms)’. ዘመዳ is ዘመድ ‘kinsman’ + -ā ‘her’ (the suffix fuses with the final ድ to give ዳ): ‘her kinsman’. The ‘on this account’ points back to the rule of marrying among kin at the end of ch. 70; that link is the text’s implication, not stated. በከመ ተብህለ በወንጌል is ‘as it was said in the Gospel’ (በ- ‘in’ + ወንጌል); ኦዮሴፍ is the vocative ኦ + Joseph, with ወልደ ዳዊት ‘son-of David’ in the construct. The words recall the angel’s address to Joseph in Matthew 1:20, though the text here names no speaker and the wording is its own. ኢትፍራህ is ኢ- + the 2ms jussive of ፈርሀ ‘fear’; ነሢኦታ is the infinitive ነሢኦት of ነሥአ ‘take’ + -ā ‘her’, and ለምርያም restates the object (ለ- marks the object): ‘to take her, Mary’. ለምርያም is spelled with ም (mə) where ማርያም has ማ (mā), so the first vowel is dropped; a variant or a slip (?). ዘይትወለድ is ዘ- + the passive (tä-stem) imperfect 3ms: ‘that which is born’; እመንፈስ is እም- ‘from, of’ + መንፈስ ‘spirit’. ቃለ እግዚኣብሔር ‘word-of God’ (construct) is the predicate of the closing ውእቱ: ‘that which is born of her, of the Holy Spirit, is the Word of God’.

sentences.l: and-was-born from-her God, Word, light that-from-light, god that-from-god, son from-father, who-came and-saved his-creation;
sentences.i: And God was born of her: the Word, light that is from light, God that is from God, the Son from the Father, who came and saved his creation;
sentences.n: The sentence recalls the wording of the Nicene Creed, to which the book has appealed since ch. 1 (the 318 fathers), though without a word for ‘true’. ብርሃን ዘእምብርሃን is ብርሃን ‘light’ + ዘ- ‘that, which’ + እም- ‘from’ + ብርሃን: a relative clause with the copula left out, ‘light, that (is) from light’; so too አምላክ ዘእምአምላክ ‘god, that (is) from god’; ወልድ እምአብ has the same እም- ‘from’ without ዘ-. እግዚኣብሔር ቃል is two nouns side by side, ‘God, the Word’ (?). ተወልደ is the passive (tä-stem) perfect 3ms of ወለደ ‘beget, bear’, ‘was born’. ዘመጽአ is ዘ- ‘who’ + the perfect 3ms of መጽአ ‘come’; ወአድኀነ is the causative (a-stem) of ድኅነ ‘be safe’, ‘made safe, saved’. ፍጥረቶ is ፍጥረት ‘creation’ + ‘his’ as direct object: the -ō of ቶ is the accusative -a joined with the suffix -hu.

sentences.l: from-the-hand-of Sheol and-from-Satan-and-death he-delivered us, all-of-us who believed in-him; he-drew-us to his-father and-raised-us into the-heavens, his-throne, that we-may-be his-heirs;
sentences.i: He delivered us from the hand of Sheol, and from Satan and death, all of us who believed in him; he drew us to his Father and raised us into the heavens, his throne, that we might be his heirs;
sentences.n: ባልሐነ is the perfect 3ms of ባልሐ ‘deliver, set free’ + -ነ ‘us’. ወእምሰይጣንወእሞት is two words run together in the source: ወእምሰይጣን ‘and from Satan’ + ወእሞት, which stands for ወእምሞት ‘and from death’ (the ም of እም- and of ሞት have fallen together, perhaps a scribal haplography (?)); read as two. ለኵልነ is ለ- + ኵል- ‘all’ + -ነ ‘of us’, ‘all of us’; the ለ- marks the object again, in apposition to the -ነ on the verb. እለ አመነ ቦቱ ‘who believed in him’: እለ is the plural relative, but አመነ is 3ms, an irregular match (distributive ‘each who believed’, or a slip for አመኑ (?)); ቦቱ is በ- + -ቱ ‘in him’. ሰሐበነ is ሰሐበ ‘draw, drag’ + -ነ; ወአዕረገነ is the a-stem (causative) of ዐርገ ‘ascend’, ‘made us ascend’, with ውስተ ሰማያት ‘into the heavens’. I take መንበሩ ‘his throne’ in apposition to ‘the heavens’ (the suffix is plain -u, not the accusative -ō, which favours this over ‘to his throne’) (?). ከመ ንኩን is ከመ ‘that’ + the 1cp jussive of ኮነ ‘be’. መዋርስቲሁ ‘his heirs’ is a plural መዋርስት + -ሁ, from the root w-r-s ‘inherit’; the singular and pattern are uncertain (possibly related to ዋርስ/ወራሲ ‘heir’) (?). The form does not itself say ‘co-’.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ውእቱ ፡ መፍቀሬ ፡ ሰብእ ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ወሎቱ ፡ ይደሉ ፡ ስብሐት ፡ እስከ ፡ ለዓለም ፡ አሜን ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.tr: ʾəsmä wəʾtu mäfqäre säbʾ wəʾtu wälotu yədälu səbḥät ʾəskä läʿaläm ʾämen
sentences.l: for he lover-of humankind he (is), and-to-him is-fitting glory until forever. Amen.
sentences.i: For he is the lover of humankind, and glory is due to him for ever. Amen.
sentences.n: መፍቀሬ is the construct of መፍቀሪ ‘lover’ (an agent noun from ፈቀረ ‘love’), so መፍቀሬ ሰብእ is ‘lover-of humankind’, a title of God (it is, I believe, familiar in the liturgy (?)); ውእቱ twice, the second as copula. ሎቱ ‘to him’ (ለ- + -ቱ) with ይደሉ ‘it is fitting, it is due’ (3ms imperfect of ደለወ ‘be fitting’) and ስብሐት ‘glory, praise’; እስከ ለዓለም ‘until forever’, i.e. ‘for ever’. The part closes with አሜን ‘Amen’ and the five ፨ marks that, as in the previous part, close the chapter in the source and stay with the last unit.
